title: How do ruin your brand overnight
body: I’ve been a long time fan of James Clear from his early days and seen him implement various monetisation methods but honestly never expected this day to come where he has clearly lost touch with his core audience of people wanting to improve themselves. No matter how good this app may or may not be, it’s pricing is beyond absurd. Furthermore, there is simply no justification for it being subscription based other than being a self serving method to hold your data to ransom should you ever contemplate leaving. One habit you don’t want to form is being dependent on this app. You simply don’t need it. James is simply trying to cash in on vulnerable people who are so gullible they believe the app is necessary for their improvement journey to be successful. For all his moral posturing, James has proven to be just another hypocrit selling himself out at the alter of the almighty dollar. Sad.

title: Great app, too expensive!
body:
This app has been great in keeping my focused on some things I want to work on. Was pleasantly surprised to find content from the book (must read!) but I found m that helpful in reminding me things I read. The book really helped me have a different perspective of things and helped me work on some of my shortcomings. I really like how I can create some habits to focus on that I can make specific and set reminders throughout the day. When the reminders go off, it’s 1 min of reflection time to refocus in my head on where I want to be. 

 Cons: I do not like how expensive the app is. As the trial period ends soon, I am flustered on what to do. The free version only allows for 1 habit and I have 3. At least make it 2 habits in the free version? Please lower your price or increase your habit allowance. Another thing, I just updated the app as there was an update. Before updating, the habits were in coloured circles, which I loved. Having that different layout and interactive haptic feature kept it fresh and easy to use. After I updated it, the compact version just does a normal coloured box in a list layout. If you do select the compact version, it’s even uglier with large coloured square bubbles and you have to scroll down to get to all your habits. I suggest returning it to the previous circled bubbles. It was easier to see your habits and different outlook on them. 

 Please return the circles for each habit along with the haptic feature for competing the habit. Also liked when I pressed the bubble, it would take me to my habit to read. This new square listed layout, you cannot do that and have to press the + and have to go to “habit details” to read it.

title: Too expensive
body:
I was really excited when you guys announced you were coming out with an app. But after I saw the price, I immediately uninstalled. I can see that you guys are replying to the other reviews pushing your pro version but there are three major problems with this:

A) the perks of pro absolutely do not justify a price of $149 a year. There are essentially 3 additional perks.
B) the perks of the free version do not justify even *keeping* the app. You can only track one habit? Isn’t the whole point about making small incremental changes that build to a bigger end? If I want to be a mindful, active, ambitious, creative, and social person, your app suggests I only focus on one of those until I perfect it (that is, unless I pay hundreds of dollars in a yearly or monthly subscription)
C) the popularity of your book and brand may have been successful, but don’t forget: you are a developing app who has *just* released — a baby in this industry, basically. Prices should start out cheap to encourage people to just give you a shot. Tie people in with a deal: “discount for life only for a limited time! The price will increase as we gain traction so grab your seat now!” Nobody (or at least, very few) are going to jump into the deep end for a price so high for an app that has no name yet.

I usually don’t write reviews but I think you guys have a really good idea and opportunity here. I would hate to see it flop. These are just my opinions and suggestions on how you can improve. Best of luck to your team!

title: It works! But improvements are needed
body:
The good:
After using this app for couple months now I can fairly say this app actually working for me. I’ve tried countless of apps that tried to sell me on how a habit should be formed. This app is fundamentally different. The app itself is actually so simple that you might think „why would I need  an app with one button and that’s it“. Yes, the app has one button that allows you to log todays habit. 
But what made this app work for me is the identity based habit principle. When you create a new habit, the use interface asks you to create an identity you would like to be. That’s the hard part and that alone took me months to really formulate the identity.

The Ugly:
I‘m paying for this app on a monthly basis so I’m expecting some content other then the content of the book that the app is based on (atomic habits). I mean ok let’s have some content from the book. But that’s it? 

A Minor Request:
I would like to be able to create a habit that counts how many times a week I repeated it. I mean I have a different lifestyle then the authors. I don’t have to live the exact same way just because it worked.

There a gazillion other habit trackers, even better ones than this one and for a much more palatable price. 

But this one has character, which I like. But this personality is not worth (to me at least) such a absurdly high pricepoint. Take for example „fabulous“. Great habit tracker, although with a completely different design language, but still science based and for 1/4 of the price. I really don’t understand the thought process behind atoms to be honest. They must’ve thought that „the fans“ or people with enough  money will buy the app and they calculated that this will be enough profit. 

Mind you im obviously a bit frustrated while writing this, but even with a clear mind you cannot argue that this is a fair value proposition. 

I rather do a habit tracker in my BuJo and spare me the digital noise and give more meaning to my life than to buy a subscription for an overpriced tracker which suggest to add more simplicity to my life.

title: Great Design, Pricey Commitment
body:
Overall: Atoms offers a sleek interface and potentially valuable tools for habit formation, but the subscription cost is significantly higher than most similar apps. The 28-day free pro trial allows you to fully explore its features before committing, but be prepared for a hefty price tag if you decide to subscribe.

Positive:

Beautiful interface: The app is visually appealing and user-friendly, making it a pleasure to interact with.
Atomic Habits focus: Aligns with the popular self-improvement book "Atomic Habits" by James Clear, offering a structured approach to habit building.
28-day free pro trial: Gives you ample time to test all features and decide if the pro trialcost aligns with your needs.
Negatives:

High subscription cost: The monthly (€20) and annual (€130) subscriptions are significantly more expensive than most habit-tracking apps.
Limited free features: The free version offers minimal functionality, preventing users from fully exploring the app's potential before trying the pro trial.
Recommendation:

While Atoms presents a visually appealing design and leverages the principles of Atomic Habits, its high subscription cost is a major drawback. Take advantage of the generous 28-day free pro trial to thoroughly explore the app and compare it to free or more affordable alternatives. Consider exploring other habit-tracking apps to see if they offer similar features and effectiveness at a lower price point.

title: Mixed feelings - app is nice enough but not worth the price
body: I have been using this app for a few months now and it has helped me develop some healthy habits from scratch. For example - I strength train, eat a portion of berries, and do some deep breathing every day (I did none of these before the app). These habits have really stuck and the psychology of the app is great for this - little habits, you can miss a day but not two (so it's not all or nothing), you get nice visual and tactile feedback to get the little dopamine hit. That said - this is really all the app offers and there are other apps that provide similar. This app is not as great as it appears to think it is when compared with other similar apps. The streaks app, for example, offers a lot of this functionality for free. I am very happy to pay for apps and I do not think that app developers should work hard and not get paid what they're worth. But the price feels ludicrous - and there are no staggered price points. I feel the team must surely lose money from this. There are many people who would gladly pay a smaller amount but who will not pay this. I actually did pay for a while but when considering my available budget I ended up cancelling my monthly subscription even though I would have continued it if it was cheaper. It also feels a little buggy especially since the recent display update. The haptic feedback seems hit and miss when completing a habit. I also liked the previous floating circles. The order of the habits seems to change haphazardly. I liked the repeatability of the old style which reinforced the repetitive nature of the habits. TLDR - the app is good and nice to use but it is mooching off the brand awareness imo. It is not as good as it thinks it is. The price point is crazy and the functionality doesn't justify it imo.
author: helen1351

title: Good but not worth subscribing (yet) imo
body:
It’s been a helpful app so far but essentially its just a daily to-do list which can be achieved using a calendar app or bullet journal. Hopefully we see some improvements in the future. Here’s what I’d love to see:

1. If I write the same identity for 2 or more habits, it doesn’t recognise that it’s the same identity. So the votes don’t add up and in the reflections section, the same identity is listed multiple times. Very surprising to see this. Surely it’s expected that we may have to develop multiple new habits to form our identity? So I’d love to see a way we can link our habits to existing identities.

2. We can only log day/time based identities. No mention of habit stacking or any of the other great concepts from the book! E.g. if I want to become a tidier person, I might want to put away laundry as soon as it’s ready to be put away, but this won’t always be the same day/time. 

3. The replace a bad habit option isn’t any different to creating a new habit so I don’t understand the purpose of this. The sentence structure is exactly the same. Also, as I mentioned in point 2, replacing a bad habit might not always be day/time based, as they’re dependent on other conditions. It could be ‘whenever I feel like having an unhealthy snack’ or ‘any time I need to travel anywhere X miles or less, I will walk instead’.

4. Looking at the free version and subscription comparison table, a maximum of 6 habits can be created which isn’t enough. It would be good to unlock more habits if we achieve a level of votes. A good way to gamify the app.

title: I really like it, but
body:
It doesn’t have a habit scorecard feature.

That wouldnbe a cool feature to have, because right now its just an implementation intention app. Also it should somehow allow you to integrate beliefes.

I have made a list of what the habit scorecard festure should have (looked around conjure is the closest match I found so far):

Core Features

Habit Scorecard Creation
Ability to list daily habits with timestamps.
Options to categorize each habit as positive (+), negative (-), or neutral (=).
User-friendly interface to add, edit, and delete habits throughout the day.
Integration with Apple Watch
Seamless syncing with Apple Health to import data relevant to habits (e.g., exercise, standing hours, heart rate data that might indicate stress or relaxation).
Trigger notifications or reminders based on certain activity thresholds or lack thereof (e.g., reminding to stand or take a break from screen time).
Data Analysis and Export
Tools to analyze habits over time, identifying patterns and potential triggers for negative habits. (Chatgpt integration to analyse the text in each habit to show patterns, give summaries and insight)
Capability to export data in common formats (e.g., CSV, PDF, excel) for deeper analysis or sharing with professionals like therapists or coaches.
User Customization and Settings
Customizable views to focus on daily, weekly, or monthly habit tracking
Customizable dashboard to view daily progress, weekly summaries, and monthly trends.
Settings to adjust how habits are displayed and categorized, based on user preferences. You are able to name lists and organise them. For example you can have a list for workmeetings or swimming and keep track of that.
Have a constant view of beliefe at all times, probably on top of the app as your prewritten beliefes are scrolling by all times you use the app. 
Settings to adjust how habits are displayed and categorized, based on user preferences.
Different themes or display modes (e.g., dark mode, minimalist layout) for user comfort and accessibility.
Optional widgets for quick views of habit status on phone home screens or watch faces.
You should be also able to „combine habit lists, scorecards” to build bigger combinations after a list becomes automatic
Privacy and Data Security
Ensure high-level encryption for user data both in transit and at rest.
Compliance with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA as applicable) to safeguard user data.
Additional Features

Social Sharing Options
Optional feature to share progress with friends or a community for motivation and support.
Ability to connect with other users for accountability. They could rate eachothers lists of habits compared in effectivness to beliefe.
Gamification Elements
Implement points, badges, and levels to encourage habit improvement.
Animations, shaking feedback… ect to make the experience more rewarding
Rewards for achieving milestones or replacing negative habits with positive ones.
Integration of a Pomodoro-style timer with alternating focus sessions (25 minutes) and breaks (5 minutes), where users can manage their lists during the breaks.
AI Insights
Utilize machine learning to offer personalized insights based on user data, suggesting the most impactful habit changes.
Predictive analytics to warn users about potential fallbacks to negative habits based on historical data and trends.
Ai could even determine how well habits aligned with beliefs
Notifacitions and reminders

The “congratulations” habit completion screen was nice at first, but i dont need to see the animation for the 20th time that I log a habit, cos it takes too long  to load. maybe it’s better for it to be shown for certain milestones (1st week, 2 weeks in a row, 1 month in a row, 2 months in a row, etc)

Logging previous day - As humans, we sometimes tend to forget. And this applies for forgetting to log a habit for previous day. The option to log it needs to be more obvious, and be accessed quicker.

App Widget form - there needs to be a better way to present your habit info in the widget, because right now they just appear super tiny especially if you’re trying to log more than 6+ habits.

title: Preposterous
body:
I am certain that for individuals residing in California or those who can afford to live anywhere globally, a subscription fee of 17 USD per month might seem reasonable for an app. However, in Peru, 69.90 PEN (approximately 18.50 USD) is not just out of touch—it's blatantly preposterous. Considering that 69.90 PEN represents about 6.82% of the minimum wage in a country where over 70% of the workforce is employed informally without insurance, this pricing is excessively unrealistic. I deeply regret this tirade, but I am merely expressing my frustration. Such pricing is illogical outside the wealthiest 1% globally.

A decade ago, the minimum wage in Peru was 750 PEN; today, it is 1025 PEN.

The adjusted subscription fee for Peru, based on purchasing power parity, should be around 16.42 PEN (approximately 4.60 USD) per month. Yet, for every Peruvian outside the wealthiest 1%, 5 USD is still prohibitively expensive for a monthly app subscription. This stark contrast underscores the current pricing's lack of alignment with the local economic reality.

While the app is very well-developed, it mandates the week to start on Sundays (which is not the norm in most countries) and enforces a 12-hour clock format (again, at odds with global standards).

title: I do like the book, but this app has so many design flaws
body:
Hello James,

I've read the book and I really liked it. However, this app is littered with design flaws I have to uninstall it:

1. Paid users can't create more than 6 habits. This is a pretty strange design. A paid user is supposed to create unlimited amount of habits and not get hard locked to only 6 habits. A paid user pays $5/month or $40/year just to create only 6 habits simultaneously? Other similar apps use hard limit to incentivize in-app purchase, not locking them down to a limited version. 
2. Tutorials bombard a new user from the start. No one cares honestly. I just want a habit app that's simple and efficient and it works. It should give me several functions: it can create a habit; it can track a habit; it has a heat map; it can repeat itself in a way I like. Every single tab is pushed with prolonged tutorials on how to use the app properly whereas I just want a simple design that gets the job done. Yes, wisdom, yes, quotes. No one cares. A habit app needs to suffice some basic functions for user to want to use it. I'm on a free trial of this app and I don't even want to use it because I find it just inefficient and does not do the job well. 
3. I understand this is a companion app for the book Atomic Habits, but honestly the app is so littered with unnecessary stuff and hardcoded limits it feels like a waste of time to use it. People use a habit app to record their habits and understand the patterns. Check out some competitor apps you'll see how they design their apps. A habit app is supposed to be simple, efficient, and gets the job done. If these metrics can't even be sufficed, there is no point in 7 tutorials on how to use the app properly and then some. Some tutorials even bugged out on my phone and I had to close them. 
4. I have to input a specific time to a habit? And I also have to hard lock specific days in a week? Absolutely strange design. Let's just say repetition is supposed to be "any 4 days in a week". This is not selectable in the app at all neither can you create the pattern. I also don't understand why a specific time has to be put into place IN ORDER TO create a habit. You can assign a time later plus I don't hard lock a time to a habit I'll do but I do do the habit on the day when time frees out. 

What's great about the app:
1. Finishing a habit feels great. Holding the button and it registers as a completion does feel great. This is a great design. 
2. I do like the quotes and wisdom baked into this app. When you build a habit alongside these wisdom quotes, it does stand out much more than other apps. However, if basic functions can't be sufficed, no amount of wisdom can save a dysfunctional app.

title: Locked out of free version forever
body:

Also, I had a paid subscription for a while and had to cancel it. In theory I should still be able to have 1 habit on the free version. However, I’m locked out of making changes to any of my 4 habits without paying them for at least another month. Free users should be able to archive habits when reverting from a paid plan instead of deleting the entire history—this disincentivizes me to come back later if I want to rejoin the paid plan.

I deleted 3 of my 4 established habits but I still can’t edit my 1 remaining habit, view detailed history, or even mark it completed. It’s my habit for walking my dog, who is recently deceased, and I don’t want to delete these records of us spending time together. I guess the app is bricked for me now. I can’t recommend it to anyone. Find a cheaper option that is more considerate to users.

title: Habit Stacking failure
body:
This may be a niche complaint but this alone has made me delete the app. When habit stacking, if one of the individual habits in the stack is performed multiple times a day, the stack will not progress until that task is completed for the whole day. This means if you have a stack that involved you brushing your teeth (assuming you have it set to remind you twice; once in the morning, once in the evening), you would have to brush your teeth twice in one go to move the stack. This makes no sense as if i have a habit to repeat multiple times through my day i may want to create different stacks for the different times i want to use that habit.

Another thing is the limit of habits. To limit the user to only six habits seems counterintuitive. I understand the logic of trying to keep things simple but it feels like a box to be forced in. Assuming most people with this app have read the book, like myself, we will know our limit on how many habits to create so it's a no for me. 

Still love the book and i'm appreciative of his work, but this felt like not all avenues were accounted for. Need more work from this app to make it worth my while

A year later, I was auto-charged for an annual renewal with no reminder and no warning. I reached out to support the same day of the charge, but was told it was my fault for not cancelling and that no refund would be issued.

This feels like a predatory subscription tactic — profiting off people who forgot to cancel rather than providing ongoing value. Definitely not what I’d expect from a brand built on “intentional living.” Disappointed and disputing the charge.

If you’re thinking about trying this app, just be careful — and set a calendar reminder to cancel. You won’t get one from them.

title: Engaging design but overpriced
body: Pros: The design is sleek and motivating. I love the interactive feature of holding & pressing a habit and watching it grow while the pone vibrates —it’s both satisfying and encouraging to return the next day. I also appreciate the emphasis on attaching habits to identity, prompting deeper reflection on why I want to build a habit and the type of person I aspire to be. The new focus session feature is excellent. Timing my habits really works for me. The daily sessions and readings are short, motivating, and easy to digest. Cons: While I enjoy the app, the price is steep at $9.99 per month. Compared to other habit trackers that offer more features and unlimited habits for significantly less (e.g., $3 per year), this seems overpriced. I’d be willing to pay around $3 per month with some additional improvements. What I’d love to see soon: It would be great to have an accountability partner feature, where app users can connect with each other to share goals and provide support. I think that you can do a random matching, or users with similar goals. Rotating partners weekly would also be good, so it is not always the same person. I think this would foster a sense of community and support I’d love to track habits with multiple repetitions throughout the day (like drinking 8 glasses of water) and monitor progress easily. In the free version, offering users the ability to track up an additional habit (up to 3) after successfully building one might also be a nice incentive to keep going. I believe in the potential of the app, but I hope the pricing becomes more reasonable soon.

title: Pretty, but limited and expensive
body:
After reading the book and finding it extremely helpful, I suppose my expectations for the app were too high. But yes… it’s objectively limited, expensive and doesn’t even truly matches the objective of the book. At some level if feels like the author is monetizing on his fame… good old capitalism, I guess. 

So it’s expensive. VERY expensive. My mobile plan in Europe is cheaper than this app. Even Netflix is. And I don’t mind paying for something that’s worth it, but this app sure isn’t. 

Take for example the habits you can track. Six! Yes… S.I.X. You want to cultivate a different habit each weekday? Nope…. You’ll be missing one day. The habit tracker template on JC website has almost 20 habits. And it’s free!

Moreover, the way habits are formulated are limited and incongruous with the book. They have to follow a format of “I’ll do X at Y, to become Z”.  No Habit Stacking, no breaking a habit, no other cue managing, no nothing. You get that format and that’s all.

Besides that, the other functionalities, like the quotes and the community, feel so lacking and underdeveloped that I might be better off by asking a chatbot to motivate me. 

Yes, it’s pretty and it welcomes you with shiny animations but how this app has a 4.8 stars review just baffles me. Go to Reddit and read the reviews, they’re as critical as mine, if not worse.

body: I am a huge fan of the Atomic Habits book. I have been hoping that James Clear would create his own app for years. And, quite frankly, the price for a subscription is way too high. This app is being priced at a similar price tag as things like Apple Music, and or video streaming platforms that will be used hours a day. those apps manage to make a profit, even though the cost that they must pay to content providers is immense and maintaining those platforms is incredibly complex and expensive. I understand the value to investing in yourself but, quite frankly, I can do more with a pencil and paper than this app allow me to do, and that would cost me nothing. I love the potential of this app, and will check back in the future to see if the price and feature set improve. title: How is pressing one button worth $10 a month
body:

Fine. Then, if you want to have more than one button, you have to pay $10 a month. What? And even at that you’re limited to 6? If you’re argument is that you also basically get the book atomic habits with this app, then my counter argument is how much is the actual book? Oh - it’s a one time fee of $10, the one month subscription price of this app. 

This app is a clear and blatant cash grab. It’s as simple as that. If the app costs $5 or even $10 for a lifetime license or download that’s different. The app is very nearly a single button, with some quotes from a book that was already written. All respect is gone for the author of the book who is clearly just in this for money.

title: Big fan of Clear and AH, but this is app does not justify its price at all.
body: After playing with this app for a few days, I’m scratching my head about what sets it apart from the literally countless other habit-tracking apps out there, other than being peppered with excerpts from the Atomic Habits book. I feel bad saying this because I love Atomic Habits (and have always enjoyed James Clear’s weekly 3-2-1 emails), but I just don’t see anything particularly distinct about this app, certainly not that merits the $17/month (or $120 annually). For that kind of money, the app needs to be something special, and it’s just…not. (I’ve seen it mentioned that it’s essentially a clone of the (Not Boring) Habits app). I’m honestly kind of shocked at the asking price. Is this really going to be that much different from just picking up my copy of Atomic Habits? Again, it’s not my intention to beat up on this app, and I’m a fan of the author. To justify the cost of a subscription, I’d expect something much more robust – a whole system of guided instruction beyond what’s found in the book, maybe an library of habit ideas (optimized for iOS) organized by topics that users can filter through, mix and match, and just any other number of things that could make it more than just a phone-version of the ‘I will ______ at ______ day/time so I can become a _______’ template. I do hope that this app will improve, but it’s got to do better – a lot better – to set itself apart. At the moment it’s fairly half-baked, and doesn’t seem to offer much beyond what already in the Atomic Habits book (which, as other reviewers have pointed out, can be had for less than the cost of one month’s subscription, and used forever). The Daily Lesson and various articles are just reheated entries from the book. And limiting users who don’t pay the absurd subscription fee to *one* habit at a time is borderline insulting. Give free users a max of 3-5 habits at once, and subscribers unlimited habits. (Again, though, if they’re really intent on helping you develop good financial habits, would they be encouraging you to fork over almost $20 a month for this app?) Overall, this app reeks of a cash grab, which is a shame. Save your money, download Streaks (a far superior app that lets you track a max of 24 habits, for a one-time fee), and just keep your physical copy of Atomic Habits nearby.

title: Not Worth What It Costs
body:

A) If I want a reminder to practice a habit, I can just set a repeating calendar reminder on my phone (completely free). The app would need to have significant functionality beyond tracking a habit to be worth paying for the Pro version. Maybe I didn't use the app long enough to discover more functions, but it seems as though the only other useful functions the app provides are the ability to select an accountability partner, access to daily tips (see next comment), and a self-evaluation function.

B) All or most of the articles and tips included with the app can be found on Clear's website or in the Atomic Habits book. Yes, the app makes it easier and faster to access the information; however, having the information slightly more accessible is not saving me $120 a year.

I personally think that this app would only be worth paying around $25/year, based on how much my time is worth. Currently, the app seems to be catering to an elitist crowd.

body: I’m really liking this app so far, especially for the template on writing a habit and all the great tips/reminders coming from the book.   However, I would like the ability to mark a habit as completed on other past days, not just the one previous day.  Also, it would be great to separate out the habit frequency choice into one part that’s about how often you want to do the habit (like 3 days per week) and another part that’s about when you would like a reminder (like MWF at 8am).  Keep the “calendar” dots to just stay a full calendar with gold dots filling in whenever the habit is completed.  This way, if I end up doing my habit this week on MWSa because something interfered with F habit, I am still seeing my progress and feeling the accomplishment of doing the habit 3 days per week as I had intended.

title: Could be great
body: When creating a habit, I noticed that you cannot create a habit that does not have a specific time. To me this is a huge limitation since sometimes part of habits do not occur at a specific time. I liked the features for reporting and the easy navigation of UI; however, setting up habits that are tied to a specific time limits the usefulness of this app in a big way. A lot of our habits occur because we crave something. For example, I am most like to use social media when I sit down on my couch with my phone, I do not see how I can build a habit around this with assigning it a specific time. The ‘when’ of this habit is when I sit down and feel bored, it does not occur at a specific time each day. I also feel like replacing bad habits could be improved. Currently, it is structured the same way as a ‘good’ habit. I’d love to see some more of the advice that’s given in the book about habit stacking implemented in the app and so far I’m just not seeing all of the things that are discussed in the book as items that are actionable in the app.

title: A bite-sized version of the book
body:
This is the perfect every day app for someone who hasn’t read Atomic Habits! I absolutely love Clear’s book and his weekly newsletter. The app is a great introduction into his world. It’s immensely satisfying, easy to navigate, and I loved the perusal of the “mindset” tidbits. My favorite aspect is the Daily Habit! 

I will say: I don’t think it’s worth $120 to track only three habits. The information included is really awesome, but I have already read his book. Instead,  I’ll refer back to the book I already have instead of $120 annually. 

What I suggest is a lower price point for the current offering, or more accessibility featured with the $120. I would pay no more than $60 annually for the current version. For $120 I would expect to be able to track many habits, mindset tidbits by other professionals in the field, the inclusion of the book into the app (kind of like the Bible app where you can do other stuff AND flip through the book on one tab), something similar along those lines.

Overall I think it’s a wonderful app to have on my phone, but I’ll probably continue at the free level after my trial!
author: woodiewoods

title: You’ll say, “Ehhh”
body:
Based on price, the author is definitely banking on his fame, and most glowing reviews are probably from his email list who has been promised an “unlimited” app or whatever incentive.

That’s fine, but the app still doesn’t deliver.

“Mindset” section is an organized dump of the book that just looks too overwhelming to even click through...feels like lazy UI/UX —  should be personalized recommendations based on a quiz assessment.

When I click the “Progress” section, too many words and not enough data visualization. I got bored real quick.

Holding the button down is a cute little effect that absolutely does not justify the whack pricing.

This digital book in disguise is failing miserably to be an app.

Get the book for free at your local library and buy an app from a developer who’s studied the Atomic method and knows the proper UI/UX psychology that makes you want to use an app!

There have been many pricey things where I’ve said, “…but it’s worth the money.”

This app is not one of those things.

**deleting now**

- I would like control over the homepage. My habits seem to be in a random order and I would like them to be organized by the time of day that I do them. I accidentally hit my habit that is for the end of the day this morning and I could undo it. 
- ability to add more than one accountability partner would be nice and maybe the ability to invite them via text.

Thanks again!

title: Wanted to love this but just can’t. James Clear you are better than this
body:
I was a beta tester for this app and I so badly wanted to love it. I am a huge fan of James Clear and the Atomic Habits book but this app is so badly designed that it makes habit tracking unpleasant.  In the e-mail sent this morning to announce the ‘general availability’ of this app they specifically asked the testers to come out here and “overcome outdated reviews” - in other words, astroturf. I took that as my cue to come out here and tell the truth. 

I submitted numerous pieces of beta feedback that were never addressed. I even submitted one this morning before they released it!  Here is a smattering of the problems with this app:

Streaks don’t work.  I had a streak of 8 days on one habit but the app told me it was 5.  I have now been unable to do that habit for the past week and it still says 5.  They have been told.  This has not been addressed.
While we’re on the topic of habit tracking It is possible to have a habit scheduled to accomplish 3 days a week (M/W/F) and to actually do the habit activity 4 days a week (Tu/Th/Sa/Su) and have the app tell you that you that you missed an entire week.  Not only do you have to do the habit the numbers of times you say - you have to do it on the exact days you said you would, or you don’t meet your goal.
Oh - by the way - you can only record a habit for one day ago.  So heaven forbid you lose or break your phone and have to go without for a few days - you will never get your streak back.  This app has tons of ways for you to fail and very few for you to succeed.
The app REQUIRES internet access.  This is absolutely ridiculous.  I have one of my habits as “Don’t eat after 8pm” - well yesterday I was on a plane at 8pm - disconnected - and couldn’t log my habit because I wasn’t connected.  Like why in the world does ‘ticking a box’ require connectivity!  Again - don’t ever take this on a disconnected vacation or a hike in the woods - you’ll lose all your streaks and not even be able to log anything.  In the current version of the app a large “No Internet” banner covers the majority of the controls, too.  
Oh - and if I understand correctly - you get ONE habit to track with the free version and THREE habits to track with the paid version.  And the paid version costs you over $100 per year.  This is such a money grab.  Just read the book - you’ll see how successful James Clear is - he probably doesn’t need the additional money.  He probably sold the rights to the app to someone who hasn’t even read the book yet but thinks they’re the perfect developer for a habits app.  Nothing more than a cash grab.

title: Helped me become 1% better more than I thought it would
body:
I have been following James Clear through his newsletter for a couple of years now and benefited from reading Atomic Habits. When the chance to become part of the public beta came up, I thought it would be interesting to see what it would be like. 

At first, I thought it was going to be a mildly helpful tool, but it’s turned out to be incredibly helpful for me to get just 1% better waay more consistently than I have been in the last two years. Is the app really doing anything that I couldn’t do by myself through tracking and/or using a combination of my existing apps? Not really from my experience. However, it made it almost effortless to start a new habit, and consistently kept me on the straight and narrow in habit forming.

The simple act of combining a habit, reminders for the habit, and feedback loops on using the habit all in one place made things just click for me creating new habits.

 The ability to keep the same habit but update it over time was incredibly helpful in expanding it more and more to make further progress in the habit of using Getting Things Done in my daily life. I got to start a habit, then refine it over time to make sure I could actually do it, and that I would actually make progress. Not the biggest feature in the app, but one that was very helpful for me. 

Another thing I like is the periodic feedback loops in your habit tracking which keeps you thinking on the habit to make sure it doesn’t become too automatic.

For those worried about the price, I would just try the basic features to see if it’s something worthwhile for your long term usage. It is on the pricey side for someone who’s not going to be developing habits consistently, but the fact that I’ve made two new habits and reduced a negative habit in a little more than a month gives me enough justification to commit to using the app. The price of $119.99 is worth me becoming 1% better each month.

body: If you loved the book by James Clear for its bite sized wisdom (atomic?) then you will find this app the perfect aid to put those lessons in to practice. Keeps it simple and keeps it obvious and provides little recaps of the book as well. The Pro version is a bit too expensive for me right now, but I think it’s worth it given so much we waste otherwise.
author: Reggie812

title: I really want to love it…
body: …but you can’t make more than ONE habit unless you pay $120 a year for the app. Aside from that, the color palette and graphics are lovely and strike a nice balance between cheerful and calm. I enjoyed the book and would love to use it to help my financial and spiritual habits, but cannot afford a $120 app that does the same thing many free apps (like Fabulous and Structured) have done for years.

title: Incredible app
body: I’ve tried several other habit-tracking apps over the years, and I always fall into my same bad habits. This app perfectly distills the points from Atomic Habits into an app. I love it.
author: hacobok

title: Too expensive and not enough habits
body: I loved the book by Clear, and he is such a stunning writer. Which is why I was disappointed in this app where you could only track a max of 3 habits at a time, and only if you pay $119 a year! It would simply be better to follow his advice in the book, and track your own habits through a journal or other better apps.
author: ducklore

title: Great Idea, low impact.
body:
I’m sure this app could help a lot of people! It’s well designed in the way it prompts you with knowledge and mindset facts as you create the habit through the UI. 
 
Sadly though if you have more than 1 habit and want to use it, you’ll be committing to $100+ a year. To me that’s insanely excessive for an app to track and improve habits - though I can see the dev has continued to respond with all the other frills of the app, which is great for those who can afford and desire it. But for just a habit tracker that price is steep. 

It seems allowing even just 3-4 habits on the free version, or offering a lower paid tier would improve the apps total impact by increasing accessibility to those people that can’t quite afford that high yearly cost, but want to make a life change.

author: JohnLu0x

title: On its way to the top
body: I’ve read “Atomic Habits” and one of my big struggles is that I would try to take on too much and get burned out before the first week was done. With this system, you can only add a second habit after you’ve done your first 1 at least 3 times. It forces your to slow down and actually develop at a comfortable pace. Since these are small but mighty habits, it’s worth taking the 3 days of repetition to get it right. I stand by this app 100%. I had some glitches when playing around with it on launch day, and I’m confident they will be ironed out in time. I highly encourage everyone to be patient with the app, I think you will find it worth it in the long run.

title: Great app with a hefty price tag
body:
The atoms app is a sure winner in the habits tracking/building apps but the price tag gave me a bit of a fright and it made me reconsider doing the trial because living in South Africa the monthly price is not an easy amount for most to pay over. This is almost double a Netflix subscription. 

I was very excited to try this out when I got the mail from James, but I guess this is aimed at a very specific market, and unfortunately I am not part of that market… yet! :)

title: Not worth it
body: I paid for your book. Now you expect users to pay $220 a year to track 3 habits with pro. There are a thousand habit trackers out there,many of which are free. I understand that developing an app comes with costs and you want to make a profit, but do you really need a profit with something as simple as a habit tracking app by price gouging your readers when you can already buy anything you want, when you’re known world wide. It just comes off as greedy. It could’ve been free and attracted more people to buy your books. I would rather write them down on a piece of paper.

title: Delighted there's an app

Tested it in beta and I love the clean design and simplicity and the gamification that rewards you with ability to record more habits by recording habits. Well done James.
